## Top picks for pool or beach

**Best overall: JBL Charge 6** (about $130-$150)
- It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and 40W of power. It can also charge your phone. What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and BestProducts also picked it as best overall.
- Prices listed: $129.99 at Walmart, $149.95 at Amazon. [What Hi-Fi's list with buy links](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

**Best for loud pool parties: JBL Boombox 4**
- RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It's built for long immersion, floats, and gets loud, with over 40 hours of battery. The downside is narrow directivity, so it sounds muffled off to the sides. It's also big. [RTINGS review with buy links](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**Best 360° sound: Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM**
- Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range pick. It's IP67, floats, and sounds consistent wherever you sit or swim. Battery is shorter, at about 15 hours. [Tom's Guide list with buy links](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)

**Best budget: Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4** (about $65)
- It's IP67, floats, and has 14 hours of battery. BestProducts listed it at $65 on Amazon. It's smaller, so it doesn't get as loud. [BestProducts list with buy links](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Best tiny/cheap: JBL Go 5** (about $40)
- It's IP67 and soap-sized, with up to 8 hours of battery. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

**Best for a backpack: JBL Grip** (about $100)
- Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's IP68, about 0.85 lb, and has 12 hours of battery. The mesh can trap dust. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)

**Big floating party speaker: Soundcore Boom 2 Plus**
- It's 100 W, IPX7, floats, and has up to 20 hours of battery at half volume with BassUp on and lights off. It weighs 3.8 kg (about 8.4 lb). The list price is $249.99, or $200 with code AFSC20, which the Dealectric page says it tested in Soundcore's cart on 2026-10-22. [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus)
- The IPX7 rating has no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach. The cheaper Soundcore Boom 2 ($110 per BestProducts) is the same story.

## Quick advice
- Look for IP67 or IP68 for the pool and beach. Sand is the reason to prefer the "6" or higher dust rating.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse the speaker with fresh water after use, keep the charging port closed, and dry it fully before charging (RTINGS, iTechGuides).
- If you want one pick, I'd go with the **JBL Charge 6** for most people, or the **WONDERBOOM 4** if you want to spend less.

Only the Soundcore link goes straight to a store. For the others, the linked reviews have the current retailer buttons, and prices change, so check them at checkout.
